rows.title: The set 2 SessionKeyManager keeps the pinned EIP-712 domain; the domain's verifying contract is the Exchange, not the SessionKeyManager
rows.precondition: a signature produced against the pinned domain ahead of the upgrade
rows.trigger: submit the same signature to the set 2 SessionKeyManager by any allowed caller
rows.impact: no impact: no replay or invalidation window opens at the upgrade, because the domain is derived from chainId, the authorized caller (the Exchange proxy, which never changes address) and the initialization-time name and version
rows.evidence_tier: exact-runtime replay of the live configuration plus a live head read
rows.missing_observation: none for the domain itself; a live call trace through the set 2 close was not obtained

rows.title: One nonce bitmap word serves every intent class; the class boundary is the EIP-712 typehash, not the nonce
rows.precondition: a nonce bit already consumed by any intent class
rows.trigger: submit a validly signed open, close, withdrawal or session-key registration with the same nonce
rows.impact: no unauthorized state change: every class is rejected with InvalidNonce (0x756688fe); the next bitmap word reuses the same bit index without interference; the mapping is per user
rows.evidence_tier: exact-runtime replay
rows.missing_observation: none; the per-class struct hash boundaries are also covered by the 26-case base suite

rows.title: Session key expiry is inclusive at the block timestamp, the associated address is metadata rather than a signer, and revocation is immediate
rows.precondition: a registered session key word
rows.trigger: close by signature at expiry equal to the block timestamp, with a non-zero associated address, and after revokeSessionKey
rows.impact: no impact beyond a one-second boundary; a key whose word carries a non-zero associated address is still verified against the registered key only, so the field cannot be used to authorize an unexpected signer
rows.evidence_tier: exact-runtime replay
rows.missing_observation: the intended product meaning of the associated address remains unresolved

rows.title: Only the stored signed-intent caller may submit open or close; the signed withdrawal path has no caller gate
rows.precondition: Exchange slot 88 holds the BatchExecutor and the new slot 89 holds the keeper
rows.trigger: call openPositionBySig/closeBySig from an outsider or the keeper, and withdrawToCoreBySig from an outsider
rows.impact: no state change for the gated paths (0xda96f0b6 before any nonce write); the withdrawal path stays permissionlessly relayable but still requires the user's signature, and a zero signature yields 0xc20280ea
rows.evidence_tier: exact-runtime replay plus a saved head storage read
rows.missing_observation: whether a later governance call repointed the keeper slot

rows.title: No selector the set 2 upgrade added is reachable through the BatchExecutor allowlist, and the allowlist is anchored to the stored suite addresses
rows.precondition: authorizedRelayers[relayer] set and BatchExecutor slots 0 to 2 holding the Exchange, SessionKeyManager and Staking addresses
rows.trigger: submit a batch whose inner call targets an added selector, and one whose inner call is the allowlisted signed close
rows.impact: no reachable state change the user did not sign: nine added selectors (claimBuilderFees, setAuthorizedKeeper, the added SessionKeyManager trio and the four un-named additions) emit CallRejected without an inner call, while the allowlisted signed close executes with the BatchExecutor as the inner caller and consumes its nonce
rows.evidence_tier: exact-runtime replay (pinned BatchExecutor runtime)
rows.missing_observation: selectors with no captured candidate are not exhaustively enumerated

rows.title: Session-key registration needs an authorized submitter and a signature from the user, not from the session key
rows.angle: D2 gates on the registration path
rows.precondition: authorizedSubmitters[BatchExecutor] true
rows.trigger: registerSessionKeyBySig from an outsider, and with a digest signed by the session key rather than the user
rows.impact: no unauthorized key registration: the outsider receives UnauthorizedSubmitter (0x93b78c88) and a session-key-signed digest fails signature recovery, so a compromised session key cannot register further keys
rows.evidence_tier: exact-runtime replay
rows.missing_observation: the exact registration type string is still unresolved; the struct hash was re-derived from ten saved digests

rows.title: The extra one USD withdrawal debit funds the Core new-account fee; the signed amount is delivered in full and no caller can influence the status read

rows.trigger: withdrawToCoreBySig with a valid signature
rows.impact: a documented pass-through: the internal debit is the signed amount plus one USD while the Core payload is exactly the signed amount, and the pinned public core ledger shows the matching one USD fee on the Exchange's own Core account with the recipient receiving the signed amount

rows.title: Any outsider can drive a victim's sweep request, which always queues the full observed balance; no EVM funding path into a proxy exists
rows.angle: D4 deposit-path liveness as an attack surface
rows.precondition: the victim's proxy holds at least the 10 USDC request minimum on Core
rows.trigger: call Exchange requestSweep/sweep(user) for the victim
rows.impact: the outsider's call succeeds, writes the pending word and queues a CoreWriter spot send of the entire observed balance through the proxy. A native-value call and any unknown selector on the proxy revert, and the sweep requires msg.sender to be the Exchange, so a third party cannot add funds on EVM and cannot create a gas reserve by topping up: each request recomputes the amount as the full current balance
rows.evidence_tier: exact-runtime replay with mocked Core reads plus saved live runtimes
rows.missing_observation: whether a Core-side top-up that lands between the EVM balance read and the Core execution supplies the transfer-gas fee (it would help rather than harm); the Core fee predicate itself is not established

rows.title: The set 2 retry branch reserves one USD and clears a dust request instead of reverting
rows.angle: D4 liveness of the wedge, D5 sweep trio
rows.actor: any caller (the finalize and sweep entries are permissionless)
rows.precondition: a pending sweep request and a proxy Core balance at or above the previous snapshot
rows.trigger: call finalizeSweep/sweep(user) on the pending request
rows.impact: on the pinned implementation the retry rewrites the pending word with the full observed balance and, below the 10 USDC minimum, reverts SweepBelowMinimum; on the live set 2 implementation the retry rewrites it with the observed balance less exactly one USD, queues that reduced amount through the proxy, and clears the word when the reduced amount is zero. This is the same one-USD-reserve shape the older recovered proxies used to get their Core send executed, so a permissionless retry may now unwedge a stalled deposit, at the cost of the user being credited one USD less while the reserved unit stays in the proxy's Core account
rows.evidence_tier: exact-runtime differential on both runtimes, cross-checked against saved archive-fork storage diffs

evidence.saved_fork_pinned: artifacts/exchange_sweep_archive_local/finalize_unchanged_above_minimum.diff.json stores the full balance; finalize_unchanged.call.json reverts 0x329c2b0f

rows.missing_observation: Core acceptance of the reduced send for the two stalled proxies; the saved head reads show both stalled pending words unchanged at head 49,255,838, and no post-upgrade event census could be obtained

rows.title: The finalize credit follows the stored snapshot rather than the delivered amount
rows.precondition: a pending request whose proxy Core balance has fallen by any amount
rows.trigger: call finalizeSweep(user)
rows.impact: the credit follows the stored spot-equivalent rather than the Exchange's observed Core receipt. A real proxy balance decrease without an equal Exchange receipt could create a shortfall, but two observed older reduced retries paid a separate 1 USD sender fee and credited exactly the amount delivered. The fee alone does not establish overcredit
rows.evidence_tier: exact-runtime replay plus the saved fork case corpus
rows.missing_observation: a real partial Core delivery or other proxy balance decrease without an equal Exchange receipt; neither has been observed in set 2

rows.title: The set 2 signed close does not bind a builder address: the signed struct is the pinned five-field Close
rows.angle: D1 signature binding of the set 2 builder fee
rows.precondition: the set 2 Exchange behind the newest Exchange proxy
rows.trigger: compare the live CLOSE_TYPEHASH with the pinned one, append an unsigned word to the close calldata, and vary the positionIds array
rows.impact: the signature covers exactly (user, positionIds, nonce, deadline): the live CLOSE_TYPEHASH constant is byte-identical to the hash-verified pinned string and a signature over that struct is accepted. Appending an unsigned eighth word keeps the signature valid and the close succeeds, but it changes neither the credited builder accumulator nor the write set, and a six-element positionIds array does not make any element the credit key. The credit site still keys on a memory word twelve slots past the decode base, so the question the authority workstream left open - whether a relayer can steer the 0.5 percent fee to an address the user did not sign for - is narrowed but not closed: on a fee-paying close the source word is still unidentified
rows.evidence_tier: exact-runtime replay on the set 2 runtimes plus bytecode-level typehash comparison

evidence.close_typehash: 0x9cc23a52214afa42e1ae53cdb2e79dc2d0cd33c33faca383ed3b149300adcb13 both sets; hash-checked string Close(address user,uint256[] positionIds,uint256 nonce,uint64 deadline)
evidence.static: the credit site loads mload(args_base + 0x180) masked to 160 bits and adds the fee returned by the linked library; the block is only entered when a fee exists

rows.missing_observation: a fee-paying (positive realised PnL) close traced on the set 2 runtime, naming the exact word that becomes the builder key; the empty and loss-free closes used here never enter the credit block

rows.title: claimBuilderFees is caller-scoped: no caller can take another builder's accrual (shared-pool hypothesis disproved)
rows.angle: D2 gate on the set 2 builder fee claim
rows.precondition: builderFees entries for two distinct builders, seeded directly at slot 39
rows.trigger: call claimBuilderFees() from builder A, from builder B, and from an address with no entry
rows.impact: no cross-builder theft: A's call pays exactly A's own 5e18 and zeroes only A's entry, B's entry survives; B's call pays exactly B's own 7e18; the shared slot 38 accumulator falls by 5 + 7 only; an arbitrary address succeeds but is paid zero. The claim body keys on keccak256(abi.encode(msg.sender, 39))
rows.evidence_tier: exact-runtime replay of the set 2 runtimes with constructed accruals

evidence.static: 0x3af8: CALLER, MSTORE, PUSH1 0x27, MSTORE, SHA3, SLOAD, require nonzero, SSTORE 0, slot 38 high 96 bits debited, BuilderFeesClaimed 0x3416b71e

rows.missing_observation: no on-chain claim has been observed; the seeded accruals are constructed

rows.title: The signed-close path couples the two proxies: the set 2 Exchange verifies through a selector only the set 2 SessionKeyManager dispatches, and a failed verifier stops the close
rows.angle: D1 signed intents across the set 2 upgrade
rows.actor: owner or timelock planning an upgrade, relayer
rows.precondition: the Exchange and SessionKeyManager proxies with mismatched implementations
rows.trigger: run a signed close on the set 2 Exchange while the SessionKeyManager proxy points at the pinned implementation
rows.impact: the two proxies cannot be upgraded independently, and a failed check silently stops the close rather than being tolerated. The set 2 Exchange's close statically calls SessionKeyManager::0xd95208cd(user, digest, v, r, s) on every close; the dispatch bytes exist only in the set 2 SessionKeyManager runtime, so with the pinned implementation behind the proxy the verifier call fails, the inner close reverts, and no position, payout or accumulator state advances (the BatchExecutor wrapper still returns success for the outer transaction, which is why the failure is silent in a batch). A deployment that mixes the implementations therefore keeps taking deposits and withdrawals while quietly closing nothing
rows.evidence_tier: static bytecode check, an exact-runtime call trace, and the authority workstream's four-arm negative control

evidence.static: 63d95208cd appears once in the set 2 SessionKeyManager runtime and zero times in the pinned runtime, and the Exchange runtime has no dispatch entry of its own for it; asserted in audit_live2_intents.py
evidence.cross_reference: atlas/block_48902346/live2_authority.md L2A-15 and artifacts/live2_authority/close_coupling.json: direct close with the pinned SessionKeyManager reverts with empty data and writes 0 Exchange slots, direct close with the set 2 SessionKeyManager succeeds with 12 writes, the historical batch with the pinned implementation succeeds with 4 writes and both positions still active, and with the set 2 implementation 22 writes and no position active
evidence.retired_local_arm: a local implementation-swap arm of mine returned success for the close with the pinned SessionKeyManager behind the proxy; it was unstable between runs and is not used as evidence

rows.missing_observation: the failure mode on set 2 era state rather than the pinned mixed-close prestate; the coupling and the fail-closed behaviour themselves are settled

rows.title: The owner-only entry 0xd970fad5 moves one address's builder accrual onto another and leaves the shared counter alone
rows.angle: D2 authority surface on the set 2 builder accumulator
rows.precondition: two seeded builderFees entries at slot 39
rows.trigger: call 0xd970fad5(a, b) as the owner and as an unrelated address
rows.impact: an unrelated caller reverts NotOwner (0x30cd7471); the owner call zeroes builderFees[a] (5e18), adds exactly that amount to builderFees[b] (7e18 becomes 12e18) and leaves the shared slot-38 counter untouched. It is a value-moving reassignment of an accrual, not a claim, and it confirms slot 39 is an address-keyed balance rather than a per-call fee
rows.evidence_tier: exact-runtime replay of the set 2 runtimes with constructed accruals

rows.title: The set 2 SessionKeyManager adds the per-close session verifier 0xd95208cd, a builder registry pointer (slot 8) and a BuilderRegistryUpdated event
rows.precondition: the set 2 SessionKeyManager runtime
rows.trigger: static comparison and the BatchExecutor allowlist probe
rows.impact: the added selector 0xd95208cd is reached on every signed close: the set 2 Exchange statically calls SessionKeyManager::0xd95208cd(user, digest, v, r, s) with the EIP-712 digest, right after 0xb002b9fa consumes the nonce, and it is dispatched only by the set 2 runtime (the pinned runtime contains no 63d95208cd bytes). A direct call with a user-signed digest returns SessionKeyNotAuthorized (0xc5045f22), so it is a session-key verifier over a digest rather than a passive getter. The other added selectors are not allowlisted and the saved head read shows the builder registry pointer is the deployed registry
rows.evidence_tier: static bytecode read, exact-runtime call trace and allowlist probe
rows.missing_observation: the source name of 0xd95208cd and of the builder accumulator's own entry points

rows.title: The pinned 26-case signed-intent suite reproduces unchanged on the set 2 runtimes
rows.precondition: the adapted pinned suite compiled against the set 2 implementations
rows.trigger: run the suite
rows.impact: no impact: signature-field mismatches, nonce rollback after a bad signature, the inclusive deadline boundary, the slot-88 gate, the four-position close and the next-block replay rejection all behave identically, which is the control for every set 2 claim above
rows.evidence_tier: exact-runtime replay, both runtime sets, one harness
